characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2010 microscope; twin-jet electropolished foils (25% nitric acid in methanol, ~20 V, −30 °C)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Single dislocations arranged in a loose cellular distribution in Fe–15% Al deformed 2–3% (Fig. 5); single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations; weak incipient cell clustering with many clustered segments being dipoles
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: For Fig. 5 the zone axis (stress axis) is close to [0 1 3] and the imaging g vector (arrowed) is 2 0 0; Burgers vectors identified using a variety of g vectors generally in Bright Field mode
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the dislocation structures produced by straining to 2–3% as a function of Al content
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Bright Field and Weak Beam imaging

defect_interactions.interaction_type: Formation of dipole segments and small dipole loops by trailing from gliding dislocations; dipole nature confirmed by ±g imaging
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Many of the dislocation segments in the clustered regions (Fig. 5) are dipoles, as are many of the bowed dislocations; the relative shift of images on changing from a positive to a negative imaging vector confirms the dipole character of many segments and of occasional small loops

interfaces.slip_behavior: Plasticity is carried by the movement of single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations (disordered or short-range-ordered material); dislocations are generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Standard induction melting in an alumina crucible under inert gas; the 15% Al binary alloy is one of the series prepared by this route.
Drop casting into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould to produce samples with grain size of the order of 0.25 mm.

Cooling after solidification was sufficiently slow to allow a high degree of B2 order for alloys rich in Al and a good degree of DO3 order for alloys containing 25–30% Al; for the 15% Al alloy this slow-cooled as-cast state is disordered or short-range ordered.
Compression samples cut from the ingots by spark machining, either as 3 mm diameter or as 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section samples, of height twice the diameter or width.

processing_steps.method: polishing on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Flat surfaces were polished on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper before testing.

Tested at room temperature in compression to a strain of 2–3% at a nominal strain rate of 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.

Thin samples cut from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis using a diamond saw; thin foils prepared using a twin-jet electropolishing unit with a 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture at about 20 V and −30 °C.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; deformed to 2–3% strain; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression samples 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, of height twice the diameter or width

strain_hardening_rate.value: low; <2 GPa, measured as the secant to the curving flow stress–strain line over the 1–1.5% strain range

defects.type: dislocations — single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations, generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations; many clustered segments are dipoles and occasional small dipole loops; a weak tendency to cluster as an incipient cell structure

microstructure_list.region: loose cellular distribution (observed in thicker regions of the TEM foil); foil taken from the centre of the deformed sample

structures.overall_structure: Disordered (or short-range-ordered) bcc material deformed to 2–3% by the movement of single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations arranged in a loose cellular distribution, together with dipole segments and small dipole loops

unmapped_findings: Fe–15% Al lies in the disordered (or short-range-ordered) range (15–20% Al) within which deformation is carried by single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations and the work hardening rate is low (<2 GPa), far below the sharp work-hardening peak observed near 28–29% Al (Figs. 1 and 2).

No numeric yield-stress, ductility, or work-hardening-rate value is reported specifically at exactly 15% Al; Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 present these quantities only graphically as functions of Al content (yield stress increasing with Al content up to ~25% Al; ductility ~35% near 13–14% Al), so no exact value can be assigned to the 15% Al sample.

As a disordered/short-range-ordered material the Fe–15% Al alloy shows no superdislocations or APB faults: dislocations are single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations and no four-partial DO3 superdislocations were observed in this or any material in the study.
